findings.summary: A `.rs` deliverable alone counts as the fix signal, so the fix stage the error asks for is refused whenever it checks its speed-up by timing the full run.
findings.evidence: The root cause is a fix *chosen from* the result of a run made in the same job. Path (a) drops that dependency: any `crates/**.rs` or `xtask/**.rs` deliverable counts as the fix. A speed-up fix stage has `.rs` deliverables, and under the behavior-evidence default it must show the speed-up happening, so a natural criterion is 'Time the full workspace test run after the change; the slowest binary takes under 60 seconds' or 'Run the full workspace test suite and confirm the slowest binary takes under 60 seconds'. Each is one clause with a run directive ('time the' / 'run the'), a full-run phrase ('workspace test') and a timing signal (verb 'time' / 'seconds'). With the `.rs` deliverable the check refuses it. Whether such a reading passes depends on punctuation: 'Run cargo test --workspace on CI; ... under 60 seconds' passes only because ';' splits the clause. The only fix-stage accept case in the plan ('Speed up the slowest binary, chosen from the timings of ... run 4521') has no verification criterion, so nothing pins this shape. The out-of-scope list says the test-speed fix is 'a separate later request', and that request is the reading most likely to hit this false refusal. Fix: Make the fix signal depend on the run's result. One way: drop bare path (a), or require a dependency phrase (slowest, chosen from, based on the timings ...) in a scanned text whenever the `.rs` path is used. A second way: leave verification runs out of the run signal. A clause that times the run 'after the change'/'with the change', or that states a bound ('under N seconds', 'no slower than'), is checking the fix, not choosing it. Add a unit test and a corpus accept case for a fix stage with a `.rs` deliverable, a cited earlier run, and a timed verification criterion in one clause. Keep the 4vkh refusal (case 2) working by whichever rule you choose, and say in the doc comment how verification runs are told apart.
findings.location: Plan Decision 4 (fix signal path (a)); Step 1; Demonstration 1/2 accept cases (fix-stage-reading-cites-timings-of-the-run)

findings.summary: The run directive needs an allow-listed object word right after the verb, so common imperatives with no article escape the check.
findings.evidence: OBJECT_STARTS is {the, a, an, each, every, all, this, that, it, how, cargo}. 'Run full workspace tests with per-binary timings', 'Run workspace tests and record durations', 'Measure per-binary durations of cargo test --workspace' and 'Record per-binary timings of a full timed test run' ('per-binary' follows 'record') all lack an allowed word after the verb, so none is a directive. The open question names only non-imperative and passive gaps, not these. An allow-list of what may follow is the brittle side. The real ambiguity is the noun 'run', and a short deny-list of words that follow the noun would handle it (with, of, in, id, ends, finishes, is, was, took, number). Fix: Either accept any following word except a deny-list of noun-use followers, or widen OBJECT_STARTS with article-less starts (full, workspace, per-binary, ten, every, tests). Add unit tests for the article-less forms above. List the remaining gap in the doc comment.

findings.summary: `request_text_acceptance` returns every bullet line in the request, not just acceptance bullets, and keeps the '- ' marker, which the clause-start test must handle.
findings.evidence: reading.rs:2270-2276 keeps every trimmed line that starts with '- ', '* ' or 'N. ', wherever it is in the request, and keeps the marker. base_reading (refusal_corpus.rs:106-113) builds criteria from those lines with the marker still on. If tokenising trims '-' to an empty word that stays first in the clause, 'run' is not the first word, and a bare '- Run the full timed ...' bullet is missed unless the verb follows a leader. Fix: In `directive_at`, drop empty tokens, or strip a leading bullet marker before tokenising. Describe the scanned set as 'the request's bullet lines' in the doc comment and CHANGELOG. The request-bullets-only corpus case (5) already checks this; make sure its bullet starts with the run verb.

summary: I checked the plan's references in the snapshot. `refusing_check` and its `step!` lines are at reading.rs:3062-3087. `check_criteria_evidence` is at 3288, `has_phrase` at 3236, `request_text_acceptance` at 2270, `scoped_reading` at 5867 and `reading_with_criterion` at 6608. In refusal_corpus.rs, `INPUT_FORMS: [&str; 17]` is at line 70, `base_reading` at 106, `repo_files` at 162 (it includes crates/athena-core/src/reading.rs) and `run` at 660. In briefs.rs, `READING_RULES: [&str; 6]` is at 1701, and the test asserts 6 rules and a section under 2400 bytes. `check_code_survey` returns Ok for class 'docs', so the corpus plan to put a `.rs` deliverable on a docs reading holds. The gate placement, the corpus mechanism and the brief and CHANGELOG work are sound, and the demonstrations would fail without the check. One soundness problem stops acceptance. The fix signal counts any `.rs` deliverable as 'a fix chosen from the result'. That drops the dependency, which is the root cause, so a speed-up fix stage that checks its result by timing the full run in one clause is refused. That is the fix stage the error message tells readers to write, and it is the likely shape of the out-of-scope follow-up request. None of the plan's accept cases pins it. Smaller points: the object-word allow-list misses article-less imperatives, and the scanned set is every bullet line, with its '- ' marker, not just acceptance bullets. Verdict: revise.
